Rule: each off-axis pixel extends toward the cross formed by top pixels? Top row has 6,5,3 adjacent at cols 5,6,7. 6@ (4,0) extends right along its row to column 5 (where 6 column is). 3@(2,14) extends left along its row to column 7 (where 3 column starts). The top segment colors 6,5,3 form vertical lines downward? Actually 6 vertical line col5 rows0-4, 5 vertical col6 rows0-14, 3 vertical col7 rows0-2? Row2: cols 5,6 are 6,5, then 3 from 7 to 14. So each stray pixel extends to meet the "structure": pixels of the same color in top row define vertical rays downward; stray pixels of same color extend horizontally to meet their color's vertical line. 6@(4,0) → row4 gets 6 from col0..5 (to vertical 6 line at col5). 3@(2,14) → row2 gets 3 from col7..14 (to vertical 3 line at col7... wait vertical 3 line is at col7 rows 0-2).
